scope: Independent agent review of each full five-language season source, including reading passages, grounded questions, writing tasks and model answers. This is editorial review, not external linguistic certification or full-film listening.

issues.finding: Japanese uses 時間帯 for both time zone and availability window, obscuring the distinction being taught.
issues.requested_correction: Use タイムゾーン for time-zone references and preserve 時間帯 for the availability window.

issues.finding: Instruction refers to an earlier request, while these scenes introduce a team challenge, job advertisement, or interview discussion/update.
issues.requested_correction: Use accurate situation-setting guidance in all five locales.

issues.finding: Instruction asks what the speaker actually did, while examples state future planned actions with I will.
issues.requested_correction: Guide describing planned responsibilities/actions in all five locales.

issues.finding: Instruction says restate the agreement but examples promise a calendar action or invite correction without restating agreement terms.
issues.requested_correction: Guide the actual speech acts: state next action / invite correction.

issues.finding: Instruction asks learners to ask about priority while the demonstration states an agreed priority.
issues.requested_correction: Guide stating the agreed priority while access is pending.

issues.finding: Instruction distinguishes recommendation and final approval while the example identifies a reviewer of a summary.
issues.requested_correction: Guide identifying review responsibility without inventing approval authority.

seasons.scope: All twelve episodes: titles/objectives/tips; all twelve readings, thirty-six questions and answers, twelve writing prompts and model answers; all 84 nonquiz five-language instruction/demo sets including guided scenes and reviews. All 36 quiz translations matched to reviewed demonstrations and all quiz instructions/choices checked independently. Deadline inclusivity, dates, UTC, scheduling arithmetic, pragmatic authority boundaries, evidence support and task coverage reviewed. No audio or real-media review is claimed.

issues.detail: The Chinese translation of by close of business used an exclusive before phrasing. It now explicitly includes the closing-time boundary.
The model incorrectly said the meeting ended before the shared window ended. It now ends exactly when that window ends.
The cue about separate personal responsibilities did not teach the demonstrated information-review scope. Replaced in all five languages.
The cue now distinguishes the required review draft from an already approved version rather than personal responsibilities.
The cues now check full-duration overlap and request participant confirmation without claiming an agreement already exists.
The cues now ask about audience and purpose and preserve unresolved questions instead of discussing unrelated role divisions.
The cue now teaches the confirmation dependency expressed by until rather than a claim about experience and guarantees.
The refusal cue now addresses feasible delivery and unsupported commitments rather than unrelated experience claims.
The cue now uses agreed learning needs as comparison criteria rather than personal responsibilities.
The cue now labels an existing decision separately from actions and unresolved questions rather than defining a future agenda outcome.
The cues now teach review scope and following up without treating silence as approval.
Korean now states inability to claim the booking is confirmed, avoiding the implication that this agent personally finalizes the booking.

seasons.other_findings: No further unsupported answer, writing-task coverage, deadline arithmetic, translation-strength, grammar, cultural-generalization, or real-source citation issue found. episode_review.note: Proposal opening identifies the audience decision, trial scope, preparation burden and review; audience adaptation does not change the facts.
Weighted comparison correctly computes 4*0.6+2*0.4=3.2 and 3*0.6+4*0.4=3.4, keeps the coverage minimum separate and states fictional evidence limits.
Counts and denominators yield 20% and 12.5%, a 7.5 percentage-point drop; raw halving and causal uncertainty are clearly distinguished.
Recommendation scope follows a desktop trial and explicitly retains mobile-device and maintenance gaps before wider use.
Implementation sequencing distinguishes approval, internal testing, resolved issues, sponsor approval and accepted owner availability.
Challenging cost questions are clarified by scope, answered within known estimates, and assigned a bounded follow-up without a guarantee.
Meeting record accurately separates an approved reception-only trial from discussed expansion, with open risk, accepted owner and correction request.
Resource negotiation preserves the review requirement and conditions broader scope on confirmed reviewer availability; smaller trial tradeoffs are explicit.
Self-review distinguishes evidenced personal work from team achievement and converts late updates into a reviewable handoff behavior.
Development request combines staged practice, benefit, work coverage and feedback without promising promotion.
Networking follow-up is permission-based, bounded to one focused question, excludes private documents and makes declining easy.
Final proposal combines prior evidence, tradeoffs, bounded recommendation, reviewer condition, open usability risk and separate expansion approval.

seasons.limits: Source semantic review only; no assertion about audio pronunciation or complete encoded-video playback. Production QA remains separate.
